subject: Physics
scope_summary: Imported candidate for Newton's Laws of Motion & Free Body Diagrams. No authority is carried; every gap below must be authored before this can be admitted.

buckets.title: Newton's Laws of Motion & Free Body Diagrams

microtopics.title: Newton's Laws of Motion & Free Body Diagrams
entry_assumptions: **Inertial Reference Frame Precondition**: Newton's First and Second Laws ($\sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}$) are valid **if and only if** evaluated in an inertial reference frame. In a frame accelerating with acceleration $\vec{a}_0$, an observer must introduce fictitious pseudo forces $\vec{F}_{\text{pseudo}} = -m\vec{a}_0$.

**Action-Reaction Pair Invariant**: Newton's Third Law forces $\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}$ act on **two different interacting bodies**, never on the same body. They never cancel in a single-body free body diagram.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Inertia as the intrinsic resistance of mass to changes in its velocity vector ($\vec{v} = \text{const} \iff \sum \vec{F} = 0$).

teaching_path.action: Systematic FBD isolation: (1) Choose boundary of interest, (2) Draw coordinate axes along expected acceleration, (3) Enumerate all contact forces (normal, friction, tension) and long-range forces (gravity), (4) Project along axes: $\sum F_x = m a_x, \sum F_y = m a_y$.
Selection of non-inertial reference frame with pseudo force vs. inertial laboratory frame.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming $N = mg$ on an incline or when an external angled force acts.
misconceptions.repair: Normal force is a contact constraint determined by dynamic balance: $\sum F_{\perp} = 0 \implies N = mg \cos\theta \pm F_{\text{ext}}\sin\phi$.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Arguing a horse cannot pull a cart because the cart pulls back on the horse with equal and opposite force.
misconceptions.repair: The forward force on the cart is exerted by the horse; the backward force on the horse is exerted by the cart. Since they act on different bodies, each body accelerates according to the net force acting on *it*.
